title: Patient-centered developtment of a holistic care model for people living with heart disease - A quantitative survey of patient preferences
summary:
All people with heart failure should have access to palliative care. However, it is still unclear what exactly palliative care for people with heart failure should look like.
To develop new palliative care services, it is important to understand what matters most to those affected.
That’s why we are conducting a survey in which we ask people with heart failure how important they consider various aspects of palliative care.

interventions.name:
Cross-sectional survey among patients with stable, symptomatic heart failure without a Left Ventricular Assist Device (LVAD) (n=150)
-Agreement with various approaches to the integration of palliative care
-Attitudes toward the naming of the palliative care service 
-Demographic data
-Heart fail

-Agreement with various approaches to the integration of palliative care

-Heart failure

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- symptomatic heart faiilure (NYHA II-IV) 
- no urgent hospitalizations within the last 3 months 
- regarding Patients with LVAD: implantation was longer than 3 months ago
Exclusion criteria:
- insufficient German language proficiency for completing the survey
